sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Wunstorf has two parking stories: the town centre, with cheap paid and free parking, and the Steinhuder Meer, where day tourists are being charged more. The city's April 2023 leaflet, now about three and a half years old, lists about 327 paid centre spaces at 1 euro an hour with no time limit and about 97 at 1 euro an hour limited to one hour, charged Monday to Friday 09:00 to 16:00 with free parking afterwards and on Saturdays; it also lists 312 free spaces and 15 disc spaces [8]. Hybrid and electric vehicles are charged like others, except the e-vehicle spaces at Nordwall [10]. On 10 February 2026 the council's finance committee backed raising Steinhude parking fees to 1 euro per half hour on strip parking and 2 euros per hour on car parks, aimed at charging day tourists more, although the local council of Steinhude had rejected the proposal by a large majority; five roadside streets were exempted [11]. The council followed on 25 February with one no vote, and the local weekly reported tariffs including 10 euros for over four hours at Bruchdamm and 3 euros for the first hour at Meerstraße, without an effective date [12]. In September 2026 the administration concluded that a blanket free parking permit for care services, GPs on house calls and pharmacy vehicles is ruled out; exceptions for care services are possible but chargeable [15].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is at the station. Region Hannover modernises park-and-ride and bike-and-ride facilities and passes them into the ownership of the municipality; a state climate-planning profile calls Wunstorf station, with 12,500 boardings and alightings, the most attractive rail hub in the Region apart from Hannover Hauptbahnhof [1]. About 1,150 bike spaces existed at the station when two automated bike towers for 244 more bikes were built, which the profile says reduces park-and-ride traffic [2]; the towers are meant to be free for GVH season-ticket holders with a 20 percent quota for spontaneous users [3]. A city presentation of August 2024 gives the towers a cost of 1.9 million euros, with 500,000 euros of federal and 150,000 of state funding, and says new racks brought 1,000 stands [4]. The Radverkehrskonzept adopted on 19 June 2024 centres on a 12.5 km cycle priority route [5]. In 2020 a Region programme listed multi-storey park-and-ride facilities at Wunstorf as something that should emerge in coming years, subject to funding; we found no evidence of a multi-storey being built there [7]. The Region announced occupancy sensors for the Wunstorf commuter car parks in November 2023 [6].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Deutsche Bahn's station page lists five open, always-accessible car parks at Wunstorf station, together about 698 spaces, and states no tariff [0]. In the centre, the C&A deck and the Stadtsparkasse garage have about 50 spaces each, and Nordwall and Am Alten Markt use mobile payment only [9]. We found no current EV charging count.

Our data cover the two station park-and-rides, P+R Wunstorf Nord (381 spaces) and Süd (326), 707 spaces, measured since 26 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 36% on weekdays and 26% at weekends, weighted by spaces, a commuter pattern. Nord averaged 38% on weekdays and peaked at 88% on a Thursday morning, Süd 34% and 79% on a Tuesday morning. This leaves plenty of room even at the peak. About four weeks of data.
